summary: The Tax Relief for Fraud Victims Act amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow broader federal tax deductions for personal casualty and theft losses. It removes previous restrictions that limited such deductions primarily to federally or state-declared disaster areas. It also provides specific tax relief measures for victims of theft involving fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation, including choices on when to claim losses, extended deadlines for tax refunds, penalty waivers and repayment options for early retirement plan distributions tied to fraud losses, and a processing deadline for the Treasury.

affected_groups.effect: Can claim deductions for personal casualty losses without needing the loss to originate from a declared disaster area.
affected_groups.group: Taxpayers experiencing personal casualty or theft losses

affected_groups.effect: Can choose to claim deductions in the year the loss occurred, receive extended deadlines for refund claims, and benefit from removed refund amount restrictions.
affected_groups.group: Victims of theft involving fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation

affected_groups.effect: Have the 10 percent early distribution penalty waived, receive an extended period to file related refund claims, and are given a one-year window to repay the distributed amounts.
affected_groups.group: Individuals who took early retirement plan distributions due to fraud-related theft losses

affected_groups.effect: Granted specific provisions extending the period of limitation for credit or refund claims relative to concrete foundation damage.
affected_groups.group: Taxpayers with pyrrhotite-related personal casualty losses

key_provisions: Repeals the limitation that restricted personal casualty loss deductions to losses arising from declared disasters or to the extent they offset personal casualty gains.
Allows taxpayers to elect to claim a tax deduction for theft losses involving fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation in either the year the loss occurs or the year it is discovered.
Extends the refund claim deadline for fraud-related theft losses to no earlier than one year after the loss is discovered and eliminates certain refund amount restrictions.
Waives the 10 percent early withdrawal penalty for distributions from qualified retirement plans related to fraud or deceit theft losses for which a deduction is allowed.
Allows individuals one year from the day after discovering a fraud-related theft loss to repay early retirement plan distributions related to that loss.
Requires the Secretary of the Treasury to process specified personal casualty loss or retirement distribution refund claims within two years of filing.
missing_information: Exact estimates of the revenue impact or cost to the federal government.
The precise definition of how the Secretary will define certain terms like fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Tax Relief for Fraud Victims Act amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow broader federal tax deductions for personal casualty and theft losses. It removes previous restrictions that limited such deductions primarily to federally or state-declared disaster areas. It also provides specific tax relief measures for victims of theft involving fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation, including choices on when to claim losses, extended deadlines for tax refunds, penalty waivers and repayment options for early retirement plan distributions tied to fraud losses, and a processing deadline for the Treasury.
summary_detail.significance: The bill changes federal tax policy by removing the disaster-declaration requirement for personal casualty loss deductions and introducing targeted tax relief, refund extensions, and retirement distribution flexibilities specifically for victims of fraud, deceit, misrepresentation, and pyrrhotite foundation damage.
